title: Moving and borrowing
description:
A to-do list that shows when values are moved, borrowed and cloned.

```
added "write report"
added "call Bob"
1. [ ] write report
2. [x] call Bob
kept a copy: "write report"
done: 1 of 2
```
hints: `list.add(title.clone())` passes a copy, so `title` stays usable (lesson 2.01).

A `Result<(), String>` is `Ok(())` for success or `Err(message)` for a failure, the same `Ok`/`Err` you matched on in lesson 1.05: `if index >= self.tasks.len() { return Err(format!("no task {}", index + 1)); }`, then `self.tasks[index].done = true;` and `Ok(())`.
requirements: `struct Task { title: String, done: bool }` and `struct List { tasks: Vec<Task> }`.
`fn add(&mut self, title: String)` takes ownership of the title; `fn print(&self)` only borrows.
`fn complete(&mut self, index: usize) -> Result<(), String>` refuses a bad index.
In `main`, clone a title before adding it so you can still print it afterwards.
stretch: Add `fn titles(&self) -> Vec<&str>` that borrows every title without cloning.
